integrity: The universal statements are proved by exact Fourier diagonalization, a finite geometric sum, a finite sine sum, and parity bookkeeping. Endpoint sharpness uses exact finite-group convolution norms. Euler--Maclaurin supplies the asymptotic. The bundled computation is corroborative rather than a substitute for proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the one-dimensional cycle, the forward difference, and the standard nearest-neighbor Laplacian.
Sharp interior Lp norms, vector transforms, and higher-dimensional products are not determined.
The 2004 Lust-Piquard paper is a plausible older location for related cyclic identities; its full text was not reliably inspected in this assessment.
An equivalent half-grid cotangent or parity-decimation identity may exist in older signal-processing terminology not retrieved by the targeted searches.
title: Cycle Riesz transforms as parity blocks of doubled cyclic Hilbert transforms
